_comment: Ground truth, hand-verified against each page. Committed deliberately, along
with the fixtures and the results.
The rule for a label: write only what the document STATES. Never what a reader
could reasonably infer. sample-invoice.pdf carries a GSTIN, which means the
amounts are almost certainly rupees -- and `currency` is null there, because
the document does not legibly say so. Labelling the inference would make an
inferred answer score as correct, and inference is exactly what the prompts
The predecessor system's harness was well designed and unreproducible: its
.gitignore excluded *.pdf and the metrics files, so twenty approved labels
referenced fixtures nobody had. A result that cannot be reproduced from this
resume-jake-ryan.pdf and resume-maya-patel.pdf carry no label and are not run:
only entries marked approved:true are. They are here because the resume type
is still unscored -- labelling one means transcribing every bullet exactly, and
a wrong label is worse than no label. Jake Ryan is the document whose Projects
section had nowhere to go before sections existed; Maya Patel is the one whose
text layer carries the NUL bytes that made a document unstorable.

simple-invoice.pdf.notes: 11 lines, one described item, no table. A document any model should get completely right, so a failure here is unambiguous.

tiny-invoice.pdf.notes: 5 lines, no line-item table at all. Its job is to test whether a model invents a line item from a printed total -- which llama3.2:3b does.

sample-invoice.pdf.notes: First fixture with a real line-item table, and the first not generated for the test. The currency glyph does not render in the PDF, so `currency` is null -- a reader cannot tell from the page, and the GSTIN is an inference rather than a statement. There is no invoice number and no date anywhere on it.

vendor-laundry-invoice.pdf.source: public sample invoice template (NYU ISAW laundry service)
vendor-laundry-invoice.pdf.notes: Three line items whose quantities and rates are written inside the description text rather than in columns, so quantity and unitPrice are null -- the document states them only as prose. No subtotal is printed, which is what makes this fixture worth having: the items must reconcile against the total directly. The amount column is emitted before the descriptions in the text layer, and gemma3:12b paired them in that order, putting 70.00 on the Linens row and dropping the Aprons amount (run 009). currency is null: the page shows "$" and names no currency.

superstore-36258.pdf.source: SuperStore sample invoice, generated from the Tableau Superstore dataset
superstore-36258.pdf.notes: Two fixtures share this template and differ only in their numbers, which is the point: run 009 found gemma3:12b handling them differently -- one returning a single clean line item with discount and shipping filled, the other turning the category subtitle and the shipping amount into line items. buyer.address is null because Bill To prints only a name; the Ship To address is a separate labelled field and is recorded in extraFields. Balance Due is not an extra field: it repeats the total. currency is null -- the page shows "$" and names no currency, and one of the two ships to Australia.

sliced-inv-3337.pdf.notes: A clean digital invoice with a text layer that reads correctly, which makes it the control in run 008: deepseek-ocr:3b dropped both of its boxed tables while the text layer held every value. poNumber is null -- the page prints "Order Number", not a PO number, so the value is recorded in extraFields instead. taxRate is 0 because the Adjust column reads 0.00%. The footer payment terms carry no printed label, so they are not an extraField.
